description: PayPal and Payoneer both exclude Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank while Israeli settlers in the same territory retain access. Most freelancing platforms rely on payout methods Palestinians cannot fully use.
energy_note: Hired, delivered, and unable to collect.

aspect: The workaround has a 20-30% tax on it
description: On Upwork, Palestinian freelancers often lose another 20-30% of earnings to currency-exchange intermediaries - on top of the platform's own fee.
money_note: Annual loss to intermediaries at typical freelance income.
energy_note: A quarter of every invoice, gone to the plumbing.

aspect: And the accounts that do work are precarious
description: A freelancer at Gaza Sky Geeks described accounts being closed and funds frozen with no access until much later, and said the account is only usable for small inconsistent transfers - otherwise it risks closure.
energy_note: Keep the payments small so they don't notice you.

description: Western Union, a relative's account, cryptocurrency, or registering a company abroad. Each is expensive, insecure, or available only to a narrow slice of people.
energy_note: Four bad options and no good one.

aspect: Which caps the size of anything anyone builds
description: A business cannot scale past the payment method. The ceiling is not talent, market or capital; it is that nobody can invoice properly.
energy_note: A company that can never get bigger than a bank transfer.
